E20.AdventureImportIntro: Choose your own PDF of an adventure or sourcebook. Its chapters become Journal Entries in this world, its maps become Scenes, its stat blocks become Actors and its roll tables become Roll Tables. The file is read here in your browser - it is never uploaded.
E20.AdventureImportMapMissing: no map image found on this page
E20.AdventureImportMapsHint: Each of these becomes a Scene, with the page's map as its background. Foundry's default grid is used - line it up with the grid tool once the Scene is open, since nothing here can know what a square on the map is worth.
E20.AdventureImportMenuHint: Turn your own PDF of an adventure or sourcebook into Journal Entries, Scenes, Actors and Roll Tables in this world. They are ordinary documents afterwards, yours to edit or delete.
E20.AdventureImportNoOutline: This PDF has no table of contents built in, so there is nothing to divide it into chapters. Adventures normally have one; rulebooks and single-page handouts often do not.
E20.AdventureImportReviewHint: Untick anything you do not want. Each entry becomes a Journal Entry, and each line beneath it one of its pages.
E20.AdventureImportTablesHint: Each of these becomes a Roll Table you can roll on from the sidebar. Only tables the book gives a die to are read - the rest of its charts are references, not things to roll.
E20.AdventureImportThreatFailed: Could not build an Actor for "{name}". See the console for details.
E20.AdventureImportThreatsHint: Each of these becomes an Actor, read from the book's own printed stat block. Perks and Powers are matched against the compendium where they exist, so they arrive with their automation rather than as bare names.
E20.AdventureImportThreatWarningsHint: The parser could not read this many lines of the printed block. The Actor is still made - open it in the stat editor to fill in what is missing.
E20.AdventureImportWidenedHint: The book heads this table with a smaller die than its rows need, so it has been widened to cover them. Otherwise the last entries could never come up.

ActionCost.Label: Make an action cheaper
ActionCost.Hint: Sprint as a Free action, draw a weapon for no action, Convert as a Move…

Qualification.Label: Training and Qualification
Qualification.Hint: Trained or Qualified in some equipment - every Standard weapon, Injection weapons…

CriticalOption.Label: Critical Effect
CriticalOption.Hint: A new option a Critical Success can pick (Stun 2, 1 Strength Essence damage, Stunned…), or every option one step better.

WeaponTrait.Label: Give weapons a trait
WeaponTrait.Hint: Every weapon (or every Fire / thrown / grenade weapon…) gains a trait while this item counts.

Hardpoints.Label: Hardpoints
Hardpoints.Hint: Extra External, Integrated or Non-Weapon Hardpoints, or weapons firing as Reinforced.

AttackCount.Label: Attack more than once
AttackCount.Hint: Two (or more) attacks for one Attack action - with any weapon, or only some (ballistic, melee…).

AlternateEffect.Label: Alternate weapon effect
AlternateEffect.Hint: A copy of the weapon's main effect with some numbers changed - Stun instead of Sharp, one-handed at ↓2… (changes and formulas are edited as JSON).

Movement.Label: Movement speed
Movement.Hint: Change a Movement speed: +10 ft Ground, double every speed, Climb equal to Ground… (use @actor.system.movement.ground.total for another speed).

DamageType.Label: Damage type
DamageType.Hint: The attack deals another type of damage: Sharp unarmed strikes, the chosen Element...

RollDice.Label: Change the dice
RollDice.Hint: Once the final die is known: a third d20, a d20 that never shows under 10, a cap on the Skill Die, or a step up.

DieSubstitution.Label: Roll another die
DieSubstitution.Hint: The roll starts from another Skill's die, the best of several, or at least a set die - the rolled Skill stays the same.

Cover.Label: Cover
Cover.Hint: Your ranged attacks ignore or lessen Cover - or attacks against you: you count as in Cover, or it costs them more.

CritOnD2.Label: Crit on the d2
CritOnD2.Hint: The roll can be a Critical Success on the d2 - with an Edge, with one weapon, when Specialized… (set it under Only when).

AimBonus.Label: Better Aim
AimBonus.Hint: Aiming on a ranged attack gives more: ↑2 instead of ↑1, or extra on top - first Aim each turn, while dug in, with one weapon…

Assist.Label: Lend Assistance
Assist.Hint: Who can help whom: refuse help (or refuse to give it), or help at any Skill rank - on some Skills, or with some allies.

ConditionImmunity.Label: Immune to a Condition
ConditionImmunity.Hint: The Condition can't be applied: Frightened, Surprised, Mesmerized… Can reach allies nearby as an aura.

MovementAction.Label: Move differently
MovementAction.Hint: Ignore Rough Terrain, or Push Yourself further for each Free action.

ItemModifier.Label: Change another item
ItemModifier.Hint: A number on the character's other items - every weapon's range, a Perk's uses…

Sense.Label: See in the dark
Sense.Hint: Darkvision to a range - only in some conditions, or shared with the Party or allies nearby.

SurpriseExemption.Label: Act when Surprised
SurpriseExemption.Hint: Act normally in a surprise round, or keep a Move action, or act with Speed equal to level.

Use.Label: Add a button
Use.Hint: A Use button with a cost and a limit, that does one or more things when pressed.

Trigger.Label: When something happens…
Trigger.Hint: Runs on its own: turn start, damage taken, about to be Defeated, Morphing, a roll…

Reaction.Label: Answer a roll…
Reaction.Hint: A button on someone's attack or check card - cancel the hit, lower the total, a late Snag, turn a miss into a hit…

effect.Label: Change a stat
effect.Hint: Always on while the item counts: Health, a Defense, a skill's shift. Opens the Effect Wizard.

RollModifier.Label: Change a roll
RollModifier.Hint: ↑ or ↓, Edge or Snag, applied on its own whenever its condition is met.

DialogSwitch.Label: Add a roll option
DialogSwitch.Hint: A switch in the Roll Options Dialog the player ticks when it applies.

Reroll.Label: Reroll
Reroll.Hint: Offer a reroll after the roll.

SkillSubstitution.Label: Use a different skill
SkillSubstitution.Hint: Roll one Skill in place of another, or the better of the two.

Defense.Label: Change a Defense, only when…
Defense.Hint: A Defense bonus that depends on a condition.

DerivedStat.Label: Change a number, only when…
DerivedStat.Hint: Health, Movement or another number, under a condition.

DamageModifier.Label: Change damage
DamageModifier.Hint: Extra damage dealt, or less taken, or an immunity.

Grant.Label: Give an item
Grant.Hint: Adds another item along with this one, and removes it again with it.

Toggle.Label: An on/off state
Toggle.Hint: A stance or mode the player switches; other rules can check it.

Pool.Label: Uses or points
Pool.Hint: A counter that refills each scene, mission or rest.

ChoiceSet.Label: Let the player choose
ChoiceSet.Hint: Asked once when the item is added; other rules can use the answer.

Code.Label: Run a code helper
Code.Hint: Names a helper a module or world script registered.

E20.TourOfferContent: Essence20 ships with short guided tours of the character sheet, skills, rolling, gear and Perks. They create a temporary demo character, and clean it up afterwards. You can find them any time under Settings → Tour Management.

Welcome.Title: Welcome to Essence20
Welcome.Description: A short orientation tour of the Essence20 system and where its tools live.

Intro.Title: Welcome to Essence20
Intro.Content: This is the Essence20 system, which runs Power Rangers, Transformers, G.I. Joe, My Little Pony and Welcome to Night Vale on one shared ruleset. This short tour points out where everything lives. It won't change anything in your world. Use the arrows to move through the steps, or the to leave at any point — your place is saved.

Sidebar.Title: The Sidebar
Sidebar.Content:
Everything in your world is reachable from here: characters, Items, compendium content, chat and settings.
The next few steps walk the tabs that matter most in Essence20.

Actors.Title: Actors
Actors.Content:
Your characters, threats and contacts live here, alongside the system's vehicles, Zords and Megaforms.
Essence20 uses a specialized sheet layout for each type.

Items.Title: Items
Items.Content:
Weapons, armor, gear, Perks, Roles, Origins, Influences, Powers and more.
Most of what defines a character in Essence20 is an Item dropped onto their sheet, which is why this tab fills up quickly.

Compendium.Title: Compendium Packs
Compendium.Content:
Every sourcebook ships as its own pack, grouped into folders by game line: Perks, Roles, Origins, Influences and Hang Ups, plus the weapons, armor, gear and Powers that go with them.
The books' own wording is copyrighted, so an Item carries its mechanics and a brief description of its own, not the published text. The packs are a companion to the sourcebooks, not a replacement.
A GM can turn individual sourcebooks on and off in the system settings, and the packs follow for everyone.

CompendiumBrowser.Title: The Compendium Browser
CompendiumBrowser.Content: With this many packs, scrolling them one at a time gets old fast. The Compendium Browser searches across all of them at once and filters by type, source and the traits that matter for each Item. Drag a result straight onto a sheet. The same button sits at the bottom of the Items tab.

SceneControls.Title: Scene Controls
SceneControls.Content: The usual canvas tools. If your GM has the Story Points tracker set to toggle mode, its button lives in the token controls at the top of this bar.

Settings.Title: Settings
Settings.Content: The Essence20 section of Configure Settings holds the Story Points options and the Enabled Sourcebooks menu, which controls which packs your players can see.

ManageTours.Title: Tour Management
ManageTours.Content:
Every Essence20 tour is listed here under its own heading, along with Foundry's built-in ones.
Start, resume or reset any of them from this window whenever you want.

Outro.Title: That's the Tour
Outro.Content: That's where everything lives. When you're ready to go deeper, The Character Sheet tour walks the sheet itself — resources, skills, gear and rolling. You'll find it in Tour Management.

Party.Title: Your Party
Party.Content:
The pinned folder is your Party — the roster of the player characters, expandable right here.
Its sheet carries what the group shares: Requisition, Mission Critical gear, and the Story Points pool.

CharacterSheet.Title: The Character Sheet
CharacterSheet.Description: A guided walk around the Essence20 character sheet, using a demo character.

Intro.Title: The Character Sheet
Intro.Content: This tour walks the character sheet from top to bottom. It creates a temporary character called Demo Ranger in a folder named Essence20 Tours, and deletes it again when the tour ends. Nothing of yours is touched. If you'd rather nothing were created, leave now with the .

Header.Title: The Header
Header.Content: Everything that identifies the character: name, size, Faction, Level and Role — plus a Focus on a GI Joe or Transformers character — and a color that tints the sheet. Role and Focus are Items: you drag them on from a compendium rather than typing them in, and they bring their own mechanics with them. Origin and Influence work the same way, over on the Bio tab.

Level.Title: Level
Level.Content:
Changing Level is the main thing that drives advancement.
The Role watches this field and grants whatever that level unlocks — Perks, skill increases, Role Points — so you rarely add those by hand.

Lock.Title: The Lock
Lock.Content:
This padlock makes the whole sheet read-only.
Worth switching on once a character is built, so a stray click during play can't quietly change a number. Current Health and Stun stay editable either way.

Sidebar.Title: The Sidebar
Sidebar.Content:
The left column holds everything you reach for mid-scene, so it stays put no matter which tab you are on.
Most of these numbers are worked out for you rather than typed in. Hover one and a tooltip shows the arithmetic — what Health is built from, or which pieces add up to a defense.

Resources.Title: Resources
Resources.Content: Health, Stun, and whichever power pool this character has — Personal Power for a Ranger, Energon for a Transformer. Rest at the bottom restores the lot. A Transformer gets Recharge here instead.

Special.Title: Special
Special.Content:
Initiative, plus the things only this character can do.
The dropdown next to the die picks which skill rolls Initiative — most characters use Initiative itself, but some Roles change that.

Morph.Title: Morph
Morph.Content:
The demo character is a Ranger, so they get a Morph button.
Morphing is a real state change: it swaps stats, unlocks gear, and spends Personal Power. A Transformer gets a Transform button in the same spot.

Speeds.Title: Movement
Speeds.Content:
Ground, aerial and aquatic movement, in feet.
These are worked out for you from Origin, Role, armor and any active effects — which is why they are read-only.

Defenses.Title: Defenses
Defenses.Content:
Toughness, Evasion, Willpower and Cleverness — one per Essence.
Attacks roll against these, and each is derived from its Essence plus armor and effects.

Tabs.Title: The Tabs
Tabs.Content:
Skills, Gear, Powers, Perks, Bio and the rest.
Which tabs you get depends on the character — a Transformer has an Alt Mode tab, a Ranger has Zords, and only a character who can cast has a Spells tab.

Gear.Title: Gear
Gear.Content: Items group into collapsible sections by kind, and each row expands to show its details. The demo character's blaster has a Weapon Effect and an Upgrade attached — those nest inside the weapon rather than cluttering the top level.

Bio.Title: Bio
Bio.Content:
Origin, Influences, Bonds and Hang-Ups — where the character comes from, dropped on as Items the same way the Role was.
The Perks they carry show up on the Perks tab, sorted by which of them granted each one. Underneath sit the description fields: pronouns, age, height, languages and free notes.

Outro.Title: That's the Sheet
Outro.Content: The demo character is about to be deleted. Next: Skills and Essences, which covers the four Essences and how skill ranks are spent.

Skills.Title: Skills and Essences
Skills.Description: How the four Essences, skill shifts and the Skill Picker fit together.

Intro.Title: Skills and Essences
Intro.Content: Essence20 hangs every skill off one of four Essences. This tour covers how that works and how you spend ranks. It uses the same temporary demo character, and removes it afterwards.

Container.Title: Four Essences
Container.Content: Strength, Speed, Smarts and Social. Each Essence has an Essence Score, a matching defense, and its own set of skills. Each point spent raising a Score also raises that Essence’s skill rank budget by one.

EssenceColumn.Title: An Essence
EssenceColumn.Content: Two numbers, and they are not the same thing: the second is the Score, and the first is the current value — lower than the Score if this character has taken Essence damage, until something restores it. Everything below is a skill that draws on that Essence — so Strength covers Athletics, Brawn, Intimidation and Might.

Allocation.Title: Ranks and Defense
Allocation.Content: Here you can see how many skill ranks you have spent in this Essence, and the defense it feeds. The Score is your budget. Hover the defense to see how it is calculated.

Conditioning.Title: Conditioning
Conditioning.Content:
Conditioning adds to Health and is bought like a skill rank out of the Strength budget.
It is read-only here — set it in the Skill Picker, coming up in a bit.

SkillRow.Title: A Skill
SkillRow.Content: Each skill shows the die it rolls. The ladder runs d20, d2, d4, d6, d8, d10, d12 — up the ladder is better, and an untrained skill sits at d20. Click a skill's name to roll it.

PickerButton.Title: Editing Skills
PickerButton.Content: Skill dice are not edited on this tab — this gear opens the Skill Picker, which is where ranks, Conditioning and specializations are actually set. One place to spend, so the budget can be checked as you go.

Picker.Title: The Skill Picker
Picker.Content:
Every skill for this character, grouped by Essence.
Set a skill's die here and the sheet updates behind you.

Tally.Title: Spending the Budget
Tally.Content:
The running tally per Essence: ranks spent against ranks available.
Go over and it is flagged immediately, so you find out here rather than halfway through a session.

Specialization.Title: Specializations
Specialization.Content:
A specialization narrows a skill to something you are especially good at — Climbing under Athletics, say.
Pick one from the list, or write your own.

Outro.Title: Skills Covered
Outro.Content: Essences set the budget, ranks move skills up the die ladder, and the Skill Picker is where you spend. Next: Making a Roll, which takes one of these skills and actually rolls it.

Rolling.Title: Making a Roll
Rolling.Description: Rolling a skill, reading the Roll Options dialog, and what lands in chat.

Intro.Title: Making a Roll
Intro.Content: This tour rolls a skill for the demo character and reads the result. The demo character is removed afterwards.

SkillLink.Title: Rolling a Skill
SkillLink.Content: Clicking a skill's name rolls it. We are about to roll Targeting. The demo character has also just been given the Impaired condition, which will come into play shortly.

Dialog.Title: Roll Options
Dialog.Content:
Every roll stops here first.
This is your chance to say what is true about the roll before the dice go — and to see what the system already worked out on its own.

Shifts.Title: Shifting
Shifts.Content:
A shift moves the skill up or down the die ladder, for this roll only.
Shift up for favorable circumstances, down for unfavorable ones. These two boxes are the manual controls; the automatic ones are below.

EdgeSnag.Title: Edge and Snag
EdgeSnag.Content: An Edge rolls the d20 twice and keeps the better result. A Snag keeps the worse. They cancel each other out — hold both and you roll normally.

Sources.Title: Automatic Modifiers
Sources.Content: Anything already affecting the roll is listed by name — here, the Impaired condition shifting you down one. Perks, conditions and effects all show up in this list. Each one has its own switch, so you can turn a single modifier off without undoing the rest or doing the math yourself.

RollButton.Title: Rolling
RollButton.Content: Roll sends it. Let's do that and see what comes back.

ChatCard.Title: The Result
ChatCard.Content:
The card shows the whole formula, not just the total — the d20, the skill die, and any modifier.
Click the formula to expand each die and see what it actually rolled. It also works out a critical success or a fumble for you and says so on the card.
Attack rolls add more here: a difficulty line only the GM can see, and buttons for any re-roll a Perk has granted you.

Outro.Title: Roll Complete
Outro.Content:
Click a skill, set what is true about the roll, read the full formula in chat.
That is the core loop. The demo character is being cleaned up now — the rest of the tours are under Settings, in Tour Management.

StoryPoint.Title: Buying a Specialization
StoryPoint.Content:
Not Specialized in this skill? A Story Point makes it so for one roll.
This switch spends it when you roll — it only appears when there is a point to spend and you are not already Specialized.

Gear.Title: Gear and Weapons
Gear.Description: Weapons, weapon effects, upgrades, armor and shields on the Gear tab.

Intro.Title: Gear and Weapons
Intro.Content:
The Gear tab is where a character's equipment lives.
This tour uses the same temporary demo character as the others, and removes it when it finishes.

Training.Title: Armor Training
Training.Content:
Which armor a character is trained in.
Wearing armor you are not trained in still works — it just costs you, so it is worth knowing what is listed here before a fight rather than during one.

Weapons.Title: Weapons
Weapons.Content:
Gear groups into a section per kind, and each section collapses.
A weapon is more than a damage number here: it is a small container that other Items attach to.

AddWeapon.Title: Adding Gear
AddWeapon.Content:
Every section has a plus button that creates a blank Item of that kind.
More often you will drag something in from a compendium instead — the Compendium Browser searches every sourcebook at once, and a dragged Item arrives complete with its effects and upgrades already attached.

Effects.Title: Weapon Effects
Effects.Content: A Weapon Effect is a thing the weapon can do: a particular attack, a burst, a special mode. One weapon can carry several, and they nest inside it rather than cluttering the list. The demo blaster has one called Stun Burst.

RollEffect.Title: Attacking
RollEffect.Content: You roll the effect, not the weapon — this die icon is the attack. It carries its own skill and damage, which is why a single weapon can offer several quite different attacks.

Upgrades.Title: Upgrades
Upgrades.Content: An Upgrade modifies the weapon it is attached to. Upgrades nest the same way effects do, and travel with the weapon when it moves between characters.

Armor.Title: Armor
Armor.Content:
Armor adds to Toughness and Evasion, but only while it is equipped — the tick box on the row.
Those bonuses feed straight into the defenses in the sidebar, so you can watch them change as you equip.

Shields.Title: Shields
Shields.Content:
Shields are tracked separately from armor because they have a second state.
As well as equipping one, you can turn it on and off during play.

ShieldToggle.Title: Active and Passive
ShieldToggle.Content:
This shield icon switches a shield between passive and active, and gains a tick once it is on.
An active shield does more and usually costs something to keep running, so the switch matters mid-fight rather than at build time.

Gear.Title: Everything Else
Gear.Content:
Ordinary equipment, with a quantity.
Alterations and magic baubles get their own sections further down when a character has any.

Outro.Title: Gear Covered
Outro.Content: Weapons carry effects and upgrades, armor and shields feed the defenses, and you roll effects rather than weapons. Next: Perks and Roles, which covers where a character's abilities come from.

Perks.Title: Perks and Roles
Perks.Description: Where a character's abilities come from, and how Level drives advancement.

Intro.Title: Perks and Roles
Intro.Content:
A character's abilities arrive from four sources, and the sheet keeps them visibly separate.
This tour uses the same temporary demo character, and removes it afterwards.

RoleField.Title: The Role
RoleField.Content:
The Role is the most impactful thing on a character sheet.
Drag one in from a compendium and it brings a whole advancement track with it: which Perks arrive at which level, how skills grow, and what resources you get.

Level.Title: Level Drives Everything
Level.Content:
Raise this number and the Role responds — granting the Perks, skill increases and resources that level unlocks. At a level where the Role's table gives a General Perk or a Grid Power, the sheet asks you to pick one, from every book enabled in the world.
That is why you rarely add a Perk by hand. Lower it again and what the Role granted goes away with it.

RolePoints.Title: Role Points
RolePoints.Content:
Many Roles come with a spendable pool, tracked here in the sidebar next to Health.
What it does depends on the Role. It refills when you rest.

PerksTab.Title: The Perks Tab
PerksTab.Content: Four sections, delineated by where the Perk came from: Influence, Origin, General and Role. Keeping them apart makes it obvious which of your abilities you chose and which came with another Item.

RoleSection.Title: Role Perks
RoleSection.Content:
These arrived from the Role, at the levels it specifies.
Leveling the character up or down updates them as needed.

Badge.Title: Level Badges
Badge.Content: This number is the level this Perk arrived at.

GeneralSection.Title: General Perks
GeneralSection.Content:
These Perks are ones you chose. This is the only section with a plus button, because it is the only one you add to directly.
A Perk that needs activating in play has a lightning-bolt button on its row — the automated Perks in the sourcebook compendiums do this, and they also announce themselves by name in the roll dialog whenever they apply.

Picks.Title: Picks
Picks.Content: Some Perks ask for a choice — a Skill, an Essence, a damage type. The sheet asks once, when the Perk is added, and long lists get a search box. The pick is kept on the Perk's Rules tab, and Change there picks again. A Perk you drop and then cancel the pick on is not added; one that comes with a Role has to be picked.

Outro.Title: Perks Covered
Outro.Content:
Role sets the track, Level moves along it, and the Perks tab shows where each ability came from.
The demo character is being cleaned up now. The rest of the tours are under Settings, in Tour Management.

Bio.Title: Bio
Bio.Content:
Origin and Influence live over here, along with Hang-Ups and the rest of the character's history.
They are the source of the Perks in the first two sections of the Perks tab.

Transformers.Title: Transformers
Transformers.Description: Energon, Alt Modes and transforming, on a Transformers character.

Intro.Title: Transformers
Intro.Content:
A Transformers character reshapes the sheet: a different resource, a different rest, and a second body.
This tour uses a temporary demo Autobot, and removes it when it finishes.

Energon.Title: Energon
Energon.Content: Transformers run on Energon rather than the power pools other characters use. It sits in the same place in the sidebar, and it is spent the same way.

Recharge.Title: Recharge
Recharge.Content:
Where another character rests, a Transformer recharges.
Same position, same idea — restore what the sidebar tracks — but the button and the rules behind it are the Transformers ones.

TransformButton.Title: Transform
TransformButton.Content: Transforming is a real state change, not a note: size, movement and which gear you can reach all follow the mode you are currently in. The token shows an Alt Mode icon too; the Morphed / Alt Mode token icons setting hides it when the Alt Mode has its own token image.

AltModeTab.Title: Alt Modes
AltModeTab.Content:
The other mode, or modes — a character can carry more than one.
Each Alt Mode has its own size and movement, and transforming applies them.

Hardpoints.Title: Hardpoints
Hardpoints.Content: On a Transformer every weapon carries a Hardpoint control in place of a mode dropdown. External weapons are held in hand — Bot Mode only, and they cost Load Out hands. Integrated ones are built into the chassis, free of the hand limit, and can be Reinforced or kept hidden in Alt Mode. Which modes the weapon is available in follows from that.

Outro.Title: Transformers Covered
Outro.Content:
Energon instead of Power, Recharge instead of Rest, and handling multiple modes.
The demo Autobot is being cleaned up now.

Effects.Title: Active Effects
Effects.Description: How Active Effects change a character, and where to find them.

Intro.Title: Active Effects
Intro.Content: An Active Effect changes a character's numbers without having to edit them. Buffs, conditions, a Perk's ongoing bonus — they all work this way. This tour uses a temporary demo character carrying an active effect.

DefenceBefore.Title: Watch This Number
DefenceBefore.Content: Toughness reads 15 for the demo character, but only thirteen of that is directly from the character. Two points of it come from an effect, and the tour will show you where next.

EffectsTab.Title: The Rules Tab
EffectsTab.Content: Everything currently acting on the character, including the effects its items carry. The demo has one, Field Adrenaline — the source of those two points of Toughness.

Categories.Title: Temporary, Always On, Inactive
Categories.Content: Effects sort themselves by how they behave. Conditions and Area Effects get groups of their own while there is one, and Temporary ones show the time they have left. Always On ones simply apply. Inactive ones are switched off but kept.

ItemRules.Title: Rules from Items
ItemRules.Content:
Below the effects is a read-only list of the rules the character's items give it, one group per item, each in plain English.
Click an item's name, or a rule's open button, to open the item — that is where its rules are edited. The speech-bubble button posts that rule to chat, so the table can see what just applied.

Toggle.Title: Switching Off
Toggle.Content:
This X button switches the effect off without deleting it — it moves to Inactive and its changes stop applying.
Turn off Field Adrenaline and the Toughness you saw drops from 15 back to 13, immediately.

Edit.Title: What an Effect Does
Edit.Content: Opening an effect shows its changes: which field it touches, how, and by how much. Field Adrenaline adds 2 to the Toughness bonus, not the total. Effects apply before the sheet does its math, so they target its inputs — a bonus or base, a skill’s shiftUp, an edge or snag. The totals are recalculated from those. The field is a data path you type; there is no list to pick from. The surest way to get one right is to copy it from an effect that already works — the sourcebook Perks, armor and Powers ship hundreds.

Create.Title: Making One
Create.Content: You can add effects by hand for anything the table invents mid-session. The add button asks whether you want the Effect Wizard or a blank effect — a system setting can make either the default. Most of the time you will not need to: Items and Perks from the compendiums bring their own.

Conditions.Title: The Conditions Pack
Conditions.Content:
The system ships the standard conditions — Impaired, Blinded, Immobilized and the rest — as ready-made effects in a compendium.
Apply one to a token and its effect comes with it, including the way it announces itself in the roll dialog.

Outro.Title: Effects Covered
Outro.Content:
Effects change numbers for you, sort themselves by behavior, and can be switched off without losing them.
The demo character is being cleaned up now.

Wizard.Title: The Effect Wizard
Wizard.Content: The wizard builds a change from the game's own words instead of data paths. Start by searching — type infiltration, or toughness — and pick the match.

WizardBuilder.Title: Say It in English
WizardBuilder.Content: Instead of searching by typing, you can choose it from these selectors: Category, Target, Change and Amount. The sentence underneath is the rule as the wizard understood it, before anything is written — if it reads wrong, nothing has happened yet.

WizardFinish.Title: Ordinary Changes
WizardFinish.Content: Add to Effect writes plain Active Effect changes — the same rows you would type by hand, and editable in the normal effect sheet afterwards. You can also reach the wizard from any effect's own window, through its header menu, to add another change later.

Combat.Title: Threats and Combat
Combat.Description: NPC sheets, rolling initiative, and the combat tracker.

Intro.Title: Threats and Combat
Intro.Content:
The other side of the screen.
This tour creates a temporary demo threat, and removes it when it finishes.

ThreatSheet.Title: The Threat Sheet
ThreatSheet.Content: There is no Threat type to create: a threat is an NPC/Contact, and one sheet covers both. The Used As checkboxes in its header tell the two apart: NPC, Contact, or both ticked for both. It is a lighter sheet than a player character’s — the same Essences and skills underneath, without the advancement machinery.

ThreatSidebar.Title: What a Threat Tracks
ThreatSidebar.Content:
The same resources, defenses and movement, in the same places.
Anything you learned reading a character sheet reads the same way here.

ThreatSkills.Title: Choosing Skills
ThreatSkills.Content:
A threat lists only the skills you picked for it, the way a printed stat block does — everything else stays off the sheet.
The gear icon beside the heading is where that choice is made. Let's open it.

Initiative.Title: Rolling Initiative
Initiative.Content:
The die beside Initiative rolls it, and every sheet in the system has one.
The dropdown next to it chooses which skill does the rolling — Initiative for most, though some Threats change that.

Tracker.Title: The Combat Tracker
Tracker.Content:
Turn order lives here, and the system hangs its round timing off it.
Stun healing, regeneration, and anything a Perk started that lasts "until the end of your turn" all resolve as the tracker advances — so keeping combat in the tracker is what makes that automation fire.

Conditions.Title: Immunities and Resistances
Conditions.Content:
Conditions applied to a token feed straight into rolls, and this panel is where a character's exemptions live.
Something immune to a condition simply never takes it, without anyone having to remember the exception.

Outro.Title: Combat Covered
Outro.Content:
Threats are lighter characters, initiative rolls from the sheet, and the tracker drives the system’s round timing.
The demo threat is being cleaned up now.

ThreatPicker.Title: The Skill Picker
ThreatPicker.Content:
Each skill has a checkbox: tick it and it appears on the sheet, along with the shift you set here.
It is the same Skill Picker a player character uses, with one difference — a player character always lists every skill and spends Essence points on them, while a threat lists only what you tick and has no budget to keep to.

ActionsTab.Title: The Actions Tab
ActionsTab.Content:
Everything a character can do in a turn, in one place: the rules' own actions — Attack, Defend, Aim, Sprint — and every Item with a cost, grouped by what it costs.
Out of combat it is a reference. In an encounter each group shows how many of that action are left this turn.

Budget.Title: The Action Economy
Budget.Content: How much a character can do in a turn comes from Speed. Speed 1 gives a Standard action or a Move action; Speed 2 gives one of each; every point of Speed above 2 adds a Free action. A Standard action can also be traded for two Free actions. During an encounter the sheet header shows the turn as pips, the tracker marks who has spent what, and the drag ruler colors a move green, amber or red as it eats into the budget (with token drag preview on). How strictly it is enforced is a world setting — track, confirm, or refuse — and it can be switched off entirely.

Pips.Title: The Pips
Pips.Content:
There they are, in the demo Threat's header: a row each for Standard, Move and Free actions, one pip per action it has left this turn, dimmed as each is spent.
The Threat was put in a short demo encounter so they would show; it is removed when the tour ends.

Powers.Title: Powers and Morphing
Powers.Description: Power pools, spending on Powers, and morphing.

Intro.Title: Powers and Morphing
Intro.Content:
Powers are the abilities you pay for out of a pool rather than simply having.
This tour uses a temporary demo Ranger, and removes it when it finishes.

Pool.Title: The Pool
Pool.Content: Personal Power for a Ranger, Sorcerous Power for a caster, Energon for a Transformer — the sheet shows whichever this character has. It sits with Health and Stun because Rest restores it.

PowersTab.Title: The Powers Tab
PowersTab.Content:
Everything this character can spend the pool on.
Powers arrive with a Role, an Origin or an Item, so the list fills itself in as the character grows.

Cost.Title: Paying for It
Cost.Content:
Each Power carries its cost and how long it takes to use.
Using one deducts from the pool for you, and refuses when there is not enough left — so the arithmetic is never yours to do mid-scene.

Morph.Title: Morphing
Morph.Content: For a Ranger, morphing is the other thing the sheet tracks here. It is a real state, not a note — it swaps stats and unlocks the gear that only exists once you are morphed. The token shows a Morphed icon too; the Morphed / Alt Mode token icons setting hides it when the morphed art already makes it obvious.

Outro.Title: Powers Covered
Outro.Content:
One pool, spent on Powers and on morphing, restored by resting.
The demo Ranger is being cleaned up now.

Aoe.Title: Area of Effect
Aoe.Content:
A Power or spell with an area declares its shape and radius here.
Using it places the shape on the map with Foundry's own region tools — click to confirm, and everyone inside is targeted with one roll. An instant area vanishes; one with a longer duration stays on the scene and expires on its own.

StoryPoints.Title: Story Points
StoryPoints.Description: The Story Points tracker: the shared pool, every way to spend it, and who is allowed to.

Intro.Title: Story Points
Intro.Content:
Story Points are the table's shared currency for bending a scene, and the system keeps a tracker for them.
This tour only opens it. It creates nothing and changes no points.

Tracker.Title: The Tracker
Tracker.Content:
Two pools side by side: the GM's and the players'.
It floats above the canvas so it stays readable during play without anyone opening a sheet.

Pools.Title: Two Pools
Pools.Content:
The players share one pool; the GM has their own.
Both live on your primary Party actor rather than in the settings — which is what lets a player be given permission to spend. More on that at the end.

Spend.Title: Spending
Spend.Content:
The arrows move a pool a point at a time and announce it in chat.
Most of the time you won't need to use these, though: they're triggered via automation, and the tracker only shows the result.

Narrative.Title: Equipment and Clues
Narrative.Content:
Two spends have no roll attached — a useful piece of equipment turns out to be in your pack, or a clue turns up.
These buttons take the point and post what it bought, so the table sees it.

InPlay.Title: Spending Where It Happens
InPlay.Content: The rest are offered at the moment they apply: As if Specialized — a switch in the Roll Options Dialog, when you are not already Specialized. +5 Defense — a checkbox in the Defense prompt when you are attacked. In GI Joe and Transformers you can also buy +1 after the roll when a hit lands by exactly zero; in My Little Pony the +5 lasts the scene. Reroll a 1 — a button on the result card. Act while Defeated — a prompt when a Defeated character tries to roll. And Fumbles give one back: a natural 1 that fails adds a point to the pool.

NewSession.Title: A New Session
NewSession.Content:
Each session starts fresh: one point per player character on the roster, and the GM's pool to match — leftovers do not carry over.
This button does the reset for you, after confirming, using the Party's live roster for the count.

MajorScene.Title: Major Scenes
MajorScene.Content:
At the start of a major scene the GM rolls for their pool rather than setting it by hand.
This button does the roll and posts the result.

GridPower.Title: Powering Up the Team
GridPower.Content:
Power Rangers only: spend a point per Ranger to give everyone on the roster some Personal Power back — 1d2 each, capped at their maximum.
The button costs what the roster costs, and refuses when the pool cannot cover it.

FriendshipCircle.Title: The Friendship Circle
FriendshipCircle.Content:
My Little Pony only, and only when someone on the roster has the Friendship Circle Perk.
Forming one costs a point and opens shared pools of upshifts, healing and assists; joining adds one of each. Draw from them here — a drawn upshift waits for your next Skill Test.

Party.Title: Where the Points Live
Party.Content:
The pool sits on your primary Party — the party currently playing — and can be found in the pinned folder in the Actors tab.
You can create multiple Parties, but there there is always one primary Party. The system creates one for you, and will not let the last Party be deleted, and if the primary goes, the next Party becomes the new primary.

Permissions.Title: Who Can Spend
Permissions.Content: Players see the pool because the primary Party is Observer to everyone by default. To let a player spend without you online, give them Owner on the Party from its ownership configuration. Otherwise their spend is relayed to you and applied on your client.

Outro.Title: Story Points Covered
Outro.Content:
One shared pool on the Party, spends offered where the rules call for them, and ownership deciding who may.
The tracker's visibility and the pool's name are in the system settings.

Items.Title: Building Items
Items.Description: The Item sheet, and how Items attach to each other.

Intro.Title: Building Items
Intro.Content:
Almost everything that defines a character in Essence20 is an Item, so the Item sheet is where homebrew happens.
This tour uses a temporary demo character's weapon, and removes the character afterwards.

Sheet.Title: Three Tabs
Sheet.Content: Every Item type uses the same three tabs: Description, Details and Rules.

Details.Title: Details
Details.Content:
The mechanical fields, and the tab that changes most between types.
A weapon has size and requirements here; a Role has its whole advancement track. This is what the system reads when it does the arithmetic for you.

Effects.Title: Rules
Effects.Content:
Everything the Item does. Always-on stat changes (Active Effects) and rules with a condition, a button or a choice share this list, and Add asks what you want in plain words.
It all travels with the Item — equip it and it applies, unequip it and it stops, without anyone having to remember.

Requires.Title: Requires
Requires.Content: What a character needs before taking this Item: a level, a Skill, another Perk. The pencil edits it with the same condition picker rules use. On a character's copy, each line shows ✓ or ✗ for that character, and the GM is told when someone takes it without qualifying. A homebrew Item also gets an Acts as box: drop a book Item on it and this one works the same way.

Attachments.Title: Items Inside Items
Attachments.Content:
Items nest. A weapon carries its Weapon Effects and Upgrades, while Roles and Origins carry the Perks they grant.
That is what makes drag-and-drop work: dropping one Item brings everything hanging off it along too.

Outro.Title: Items Covered
Outro.Content:
Three tabs, Details doing the mechanical work, and Items that carry other Items.
The demo character is being cleaned up now.

DescriptionTab.Title: Description
DescriptionTab.Content:
Free text — what the thing is, in words.
This is what shows when someone expands the Item on a character sheet or posts it to chat.

Enrichers.Title: Links and Macros
Enrichers.Description: Clickable check links in text, and turning Items into hotbar macros.

Intro.Title: Links and Macros
Intro.Content:
Two small things that save a lot of clicking during play.
This tour posts one whispered chat message and removes it when it finishes.

Link.Title: Check Links
Link.Content: Writing @Check[skill=athletics dif=15] in a journal, an Item description or chat turns into this link. Clicking it rolls that check for whoever clicked, against the difficulty you set — so an adventure can carry its own rolls instead of the GM reading numbers aloud.

SendToChat.Title: Sending It Round
SendToChat.Content:
This GM-only icon posts the link to chat for everyone.
Useful when the check is written into a journal only you can see and you want the table to roll it.

Hotbar.Title: Macros
Hotbar.Content:
A macro is a saved button that runs something for you, and the hotbar is this numbered row — press a slot’s number key and it fires.
Drag any Item from a character sheet onto it — a weapon, a Perk, a Power — and you get that Item as one click, without opening the sheet. There is nothing to write: the system builds the macro itself.

Outro.Title: That's the Suite
Outro.Content: That is every tour for players. GMs have one more — Importing From Your Books is next. They are all under Settings, in Tour Management, and can be replayed or reset whenever you like.

Machines.Title: Vehicles, Zords and Megaforms
Machines.Description: The three machine sheets, their crews, and how a Megaform combines its Zords.

Intro.Title: Vehicles, Zords and Megaforms
Intro.Content:
Three Actor types for things characters ride or pilot.
This tour creates a temporary demo vehicle, Zord and Megazord, and removes them when it finishes.

VehicleSheet.Title: The Vehicle Sheet
VehicleSheet.Content:
A vehicle is an Actor in its own right, with its own Health, defenses and movement.
It is lighter than a character sheet because a vehicle does not advance — a GM builds one and it stays built.

VehicleStats.Title: What a Vehicle Tracks
VehicleStats.Content:
Health and defenses in the same places as any other sheet.
A vehicle's Essences describe the machine rather than a person, and its Toughness is what attacks roll against.

Crew.Title: The Crew
Crew.Content:
Drag a character onto the vehicle and they appear here.
The sheet shows each crew member's Health and Stun inline, so a GM can run a chase without opening five sheets.

CrewRole.Title: Driver or Passenger
CrewRole.Content:
Each crew member has a role, and the roles are not cosmetic.
A vehicle needs its full complement of drivers to move at full speed — understaff it and the system slows it down for you.

VehicleTraits.Title: Traits and Firepoints
VehicleTraits.Content:
Traits describe what the vehicle can do — all-terrain, armored cabin, amphibious.
Firepoints are the positions someone aboard can shoot from, which is what makes a vehicle a platform rather than just transport.

ZordSheet.Title: The Zord Sheet
ZordSheet.Content: A Zord is close to a vehicle, with two differences that matter. It is bound to a Ranger rather than crewed by anyone, and it can be a combiner — a piece of something larger.

ZordStats.Title: Zord Scale
ZordStats.Content:
Zords are built at a scale no character reaches, and their numbers say so.
Armor contributes directly to Toughness here rather than coming from an equipped Item, because a Zord does not carry gear the way a character does.

MegaformSheet.Title: The Megaform
MegaformSheet.Content:
A Megazord is what several Zords become when they combine.
It is a separate Actor, and almost nothing on it is typed in by hand.

Combiners.Title: The Participants
Combiners.Content:
These are the Zords this Megaform is formed from.
Add or remove one and everything on the sheet recomputes — this list is the input, and the rest of the sheet is the output.

CombinedStats.Title: Combined, Not Added
CombinedStats.Content: The combining rules are not simple sums, and the sheet applies them for you. Strength and Speed take the highest among the participants; movement takes the slowest; Health stays per-Zord with a combined total shown alongside, so losing one Zord does not silently drain a shared pool.

Outro.Title: Machines Covered
Outro.Content:
Vehicles carry crews, Zords are bound to Rangers, and a Megaform is computed from the Zords inside it.
The demo machines are being cleaned up now. That is every tour the system ships.

Importers.Title: Importing From Your Books
Importers.Description: Turning stat blocks, rulebook text and adventure PDFs into world content.

Intro.Title: Importing From Your Books
Intro.Content:
The compendiums ship with the mechanics but not Renegade's text, and with no adventure content at all.
Three GM tools fill that in from books you own. Nothing you import leaves your browser, and none of it ends up in the system's own files.

StatBlockButton.Title: Stat Blocks
StatBlockButton.Content:
Paste a Threat's stat block from a sourcebook and this turns it into an NPC — skills, defenses, attacks, Perks and Powers, with anything it could not place listed for you to check.
It lives at the bottom of the Actors tab.

StatBlock.Title: Paste and Preview
StatBlock.Content: Paste here and the preview fills in before anything is created. A page carrying several stat blocks imports them all in one go — a Normal and Grown pair included, which Make My Monster Grow on the Threat sheet can then link.

SettingsMenus.Title: The Other Two
SettingsMenus.Content: The book and adventure importers are in Configure Settings, under the Essence20 section, because they read a whole PDF rather than pasting text.

BookDescriptions.Title: Rulebook Text
BookDescriptions.Content:
Pick your own copy of a rulebook and it fills the empty description fields in your world — Perks, gear, Powers — with the book's text.
It is stored in your world only: the packs themselves are never touched, so it can never ship in a release.

Adventure.Title: Adventures
Adventure.Content:
An adventure PDF with an outline becomes Journal Entries with the book's own chapter structure.
It also finds the maps and makes them Scenes, the Threats and makes them Actors, and the random tables and makes them Roll Tables. You choose what to include before anything is written.

Outro.Title: Importing Covered
Outro.Content:
Stat blocks from a paste, rules text and adventures from PDFs you own — all into your world, none into the system.
That is the last tour. Tour Management lists them all if you want to revisit one.

Party.Title: The Party Sheet
Party.Description: The squad sheet: roster, Requisition, Mission Critical gear, and the pool it quietly holds.

Intro.Title: The Party Sheet
Intro.Content: A Party is the group itself as an actor — the squad, the team, the Friend Group — and it owns what the whole table shares rather than any one character. This tour creates a temporary Demo Squad and deletes it again at the end. Your own Party is not touched.

Header.Title: The Header
Header.Content:
A name and a color — the two things you set here.
Everything the sheet works out for itself is over in the sidebar.

Sidebar.Title: The Sidebar
Sidebar.Content:
The game line this Party belongs to, and how many characters are on the roster.
The count is worked out from the roster rather than typed in — several things size themselves from it — and the line decides which of the squad rules below actually apply: Requisition is a GI Joe, Transformers and Power Rangers idea.

Roster.Title: The Roster
Roster.Content:
Drag a player character here to add them to the squad; the trash icon takes them off again.
Clicking a name opens that character. Only Player Characters count — an NPC dropped here is ignored.

Requisition.Title: Requisition
Requisition.Content: The squad requests gear from a shared pool of attempts rather than each character tracking their own. The cap follows the roster — three per member — and Reset refills to it at the start of a mission. Untick from roster to set a number by hand instead.

RequisitionMembers.Title: Requesting Gear
RequisitionMembers.Content: Each member gets their own block: drop a Requisitionable weapon or armor onto it and roll for it from here. The roll is made as that character — their training, their shifts, their chat card — but it spends one attempt from the squad pool. Nothing is enforced; the card says what happened and the log below keeps the history.

MissionCritical.Title: Mission Critical Items
MissionCritical.Content:
Gear issued to the squad rather than to any one character — a vehicle-mounted weapon, a shared medkit.
These Items belong to the Party itself. An Equipment Package dropped here unpacks into these lists.

StoryPoints.Title: It Holds the Story Points
StoryPoints.Content:
The table's Story Point pool lives on the primary Party, even though nothing on this sheet shows it — the tracker is its one screen.
It sits here rather than in the world settings so that it can be tracked per-Party.

Directory.Title: In the Sidebar
Directory.Content: The primary (currently playing) Party. The point pools are stored on it, which allows points to be tracked separately for multiple Parties.

Primary.Title: The Primary Party
Primary.Content: One Party is always the primary, and the system keeps it that way: it creates one if the world has none, refuses to delete the last one, and hands the points to the next Party if the primary goes. Everyone gets Observer on it by default — without that a player's tracker would read zero, because a document nobody can see is never sent to them. Grant a player Owner to let them spend unattended.

Outro.Title: Party Covered
Outro.Content: A roster, a shared Requisition pool, the squad's own gear, and the Story Points underneath it all. Next: Story Points, which covers the pool this sheet holds. The Demo Squad is being cleaned up now.
